title: Stocks Fall Sharply as Continuous Selloff Into a Second Day - Nouvelles Du Monde
text:
0 Comment 0 4 Views Share: 
Stocks plunged on Tuesday, Jan. 30, Wall Street setting up for the biggest two-day decline since August. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 281 points, or 1.1%, to 26,158, the S & P 500 fell 0.95% and the Nasdaq declined 1.1%. Monday, Jan. 29, saw the largest single-day loss for U.S. stocks in at least five months . The Dow’s losses were multiplied by s harp declines for stocks in the pharmaceutical sector after Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ), Berkshire Hathaway Inc. ( BRK.A ) and JPMorgan Chase & Co. ( JPM They said they would create a non-profit healthcare company for their U.S. employees. UnitedHealth Group Inc. ( A H ), Dow component, fell 4.6%, while CVS Health Corp. ( CVS ) fell 5.5%. Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) shares were down 0.65% on Tuesday, following their biggest single-day drop in over a month on Monday as investors continue to question the strength of demand for its flagship iPhone X ahead of the giant tech’s first-quarter earnings later this week. JPMorgan Chase and Apple are holding Jim Cramer’s Action Alerts PLUS Charitable Trust Portfolio. Want to be alerted before Cramer buys or sells the stocks? Learn more now . Pfizer Inc., ( PFE ) posted fourth-quarter adjusted profit of 62 cents a share, 6 cents above estimates, while revenue of $ 13.70 billion also topped forecasts. The drug company also issued an upbeat forecast for 2018. The stock declined 3.2% early Tuesday. McDonald’s Corp. ( MCD Earnings were $ 1.71 a share in the fourth quarter, beating forecasts of $ 1.59. Global same-store sales in the pink quarter 5.5% , higher than estimates of an increase of 4.9%. Same-store sales in the U.S. jumped 4.5%. The stock was down 1.8%. Harley-Davidson Inc. ( HOG ) Fell 7.6% after the motorcycle maker said for 2018 it anticipated motorcycle shipments to about 231,000 to 236,000 motorcycles, below analysts’ estimates. MetLife Inc. ( MET ) Tumbled 8.4% after the insurance company said the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission was investigating reports that some of its customers had not received and after it postponed the release of its fourth-quarter earnings. Thomson Reuters Corp. ( SORTING ) said Tuesday that it was in “advanced discussion” with Blackstone Group LP ( BX ) The financial and risk business. Toronto-based Thomson confirmed earlier reports of the private-equity group, with Reuters reporting the sale would focus on 55% of the F & R business and value Thomson’s biggest unit by revenue at $ 17 billion. Thomson Reuters would retain a 45% stake in the business, and would keep full ownership of both its legal and accounting divisions. Blackstone would pay around $ 4 billion in cash for the division and contribute to $ 13 billion in new debt, Reuters reported. Thomson Reuters rose 8.8%. SAP SE ( SAP ) said Tuesday that it acquired Callidus Software Inc. ( CALD in a deal worth around $ 2.4 billion that extends the German software company further into cloud computing. Callidus shares jumped 10%. Benchmark 10-year ratings were yielding 2.712% on Tuesday after hitting an April 2014 high of 2.72% on Monday as investors in the global economy. Janet Yellen will preside over her final meeting as Federal Reserve Chair on Tuesday and Wednesday, Jan. 31. The Fed is not expected to meet the expectations of the market. An announcement on interest rates is expected Wednesday afternoon. Donald Trump is scheduled to deliver its first “State of the Union” address on Tuesday, and it is expected to highlight immigration and national security issues, discuss trade deals and reveal some of its infrastructure plans.
